description: Journey — the build order of the content; its last step is gripforge_game_audit, not "it loads". Read game.engine of a Game Kit project (gkp_…) — a direction, never a gate. action=start (default): the start pack { version, active, structure { engine, kits, content counts, code }, scene, blocks digest, order (scene → playable → assets → archetypes → story → scripts → ui → validate → deliver → code), next [{ step, tool, args, why }], code (where game code goes per engine), rules } and the full content report. action=blocks: the brick catalogue computed from the manifests — entity kinds, archetype components (kit, schema, example), script verbs (conditions / actions with arguments and shorthand), script sugars (interact, enter, leave, scene, talked, quest, state, gives), quest step types, NPC behaviours, worlds, layers, events, variables; scope=catalog adds the bricks of kits not installed (install <kit>). action=points (game.engine 1.3): what can be plugged into the kits without recoding them — without kit, the compact view of every installed kit (hooks with their mutable fields and whether they cancel, events emitted and listened to, registries, collections and config keys with what is moddable or live, settings, verbs, components, services, completeness counters); with kit, the full extension points of that kit with schemas. Look here before writing anything new: the kit or tool that already does it is the proven way, above all for what makes a game complete (input, camera, combat, saving, HUD, menus, sound). The kits are built to be adapted, nothing in them is fixed: adapt one as deep as the game needs through its extension points — its config (gripforge_gamekit_configure), its documents and registries (gripforge_game_content, gripforge_game_project data), taps on its hooks (documents of the hooks collection), scripts whose rules react to its events and change data — in the project, or packaged as a mod (gripforge_game_mods); write something new only when no kit does it, and then as a kit following the extension contract; a local copy of a kit last, saying why. action=report: { ok, errors, warnings, stats } — an error means that piece is left out of the game (the rest plays), a warning that it loads with something missing; each issue may carry a fix { tool, args }. action=next: the next steps only. A game with everything in code is valid: content first, kits second, code for the rest. 0 credits.
